goal: Build a playful, touch-first creative kiosk where visitors create and finish a layered digital paper card.
experiencePrinciples: Keep the interface direct, playful, and understandable without hidden keyboard shortcuts.
Use the existing liquid-glass shader consistently for controls and panels.
Commit buttons on pointer release; dragging outside cancels the action.
Treat touch as a primary input and prevent accidental taps from becoming paths.
Prefer simple local variables and direct calls until an abstraction removes real complexity.

architecture.runtime: Browser globals with p5.js 1.11.13, p5.sound, WebGL, and GLSL
architecture.state: scene, data, and inout globals in js/common_custom.js

importantState.textLimit: 24 non-space characters and 6 words; repeated whitespace is collapsed, limiting the layer stack to 6 word layers plus the photo
importantState.persistence: Text, word paths, colors, sizes, the snapped background palette index, edit state, the Rehumanize texture-shuffle seed, photo/word Z order, and composition viewport metadata use localStorage key playspace.text.v1; the captured photo, freehand frame, and matching viewport metadata use IndexedDB database playspace-session-v1 so an unfinished composition restores and remaps into the centered card after reload or resize; successful Card Preview Finish clears both stores
importantState.wordIdentity: Paths, colors, and sizes are dictionary-based using occurrence-aware word keys; one persisted shuffle seed controls the balanced glyph textures across the complete name

implemented: The continuous p5 render target is set to 120 fps after the optimized build proved smooth on development hardware. During the initial loading scene, all 128 scanned text PNGs are decoded through a three-worker queue and immediately downsampled to a 512px render height, all twelve special-session portraits are loaded through the same throttled approach, and saved Home examples finish loading before Play becomes available. This removes mid-session asset waits on iPad without creating a simultaneous decode spike. Stable per-word texture assignments and smoothed text paths are cached, with animated path processing capped at 160 representative points while drawing remains visually live

Hidden native textarea with custom glass text field and selection UI; while the expanded field is empty, a non-persistent 50%-opacity 'type your name here' prompt jumps word-by-word in the same traveling sine wave as the frame-drawing guide and disappears on the first typed character

Glass UI label graphics are cached after rendering and rebuilt only when interaction changes their visible text, displayed value, per-character animation, caret or selection gradient, marks, or dimensions; static controls reuse the cached label every frame while caret transitions continue only until settled

The finished poster uses a logical 1080x1920 (9:16) composition displayed at 80% of the largest window fit and exports at 1440x2560. A separate centered 1080x1350 (4:5) creation card sits inside that poster at 90% of its previous nested scale, using a poster-width ratio of 0.7734375, and contains the visitor-drawn photo frame, text paths, and foreground branding. Outside editing the poster is centered. During editing, the active control column's live animated width is reserved and the poster continuously recenters within the remaining workspace. Every frame of the handedness or panel-width animation remaps visitor artwork between consecutive poster bounds; the nested card follows proportionally. Saved and cached photo-frame sessions use creation-card-relative viewport metadata. Card Preview and final download crop the full 9:16 poster, while drawing and text stay inside the 4:5 card with an 8% legibility inset

Per-word path drawing and size use all 128 transparent numbered scans from assets/poster/glyphs/png without SVG edge boiling, texture masks, gloss, or torn backing. Every scan is explicitly classified by appearance into Marker, Pastel, Collage, or Airbrush; unsupported characters retain a plain-font fallback. Every rendered name glyph applies a final 90% scale after the visitor-controlled size calculation. Text base size and its visitor-controlled size range remain relative to the live 4:5 creation card, and cached size animation offsets remap with that card so names scale uniformly with the photo frame between the large editor and nested final poster

After editing, the background-frame step presents a horizontal looping carousel of the six 9:16 poster backgrounds. The selected option is largest at center while its neighbors remain separated and smaller, and dragging anywhere across the cards slides and snaps the background layer. Every 9:16 background receives a uniform 5%-opacity black overlay before the current live 4:5 creation card is composited at its final nested scale with a true rounded transparent mask, preserving the visitor's chosen inner-card color while keeping its edge visible even when both layers share a palette color. Capture is deferred until the first fully remapped non-editing frame, avoids the broken p5 Graphics and Image remove paths, and separates the dim layer and nested card across dedicated depth units so the WebGL depth buffer cannot drop either. Background confirmation is now a single-use, session-generation-locked transition: input is swallowed during its one-frame capture, timeout cannot reopen the picker, stale asynchronous work is invalidated, and capture is rejected unless the creative session is still active, preventing Home carousel or editor state from entering an exported poster. The picker, final render, and exported PNG use the same treatment and rounded 4:5 color surface beneath the photo, names, and foreground artwork. Leaving the matching outer frame unchanged remains subtly one-tone, while sliding to another frame produces a duo-tone poster
Touch and mouse controls with smoothing, release-to-commit, and cancellation

Liquid-glass controls, UI sound engine, and responsive sizing; the 18-step color dial produces one fixed-pitch spatialized tick per visual wedge during both direct dragging and released inertia, while cadence, subtle intensity, and envelope length follow angular speed through the final snap
Asset loading progress first settles at center, then transforms into the lower idle Play! control; after later completed sessions Play! rises back from below

The idle home screen uses the lightweight assets/branding/playspace_logo.svg logo, a Create Your Own Poster heading, and an iPod Cover Flow-style carousel sourced only from flattened posters saved by completed user sessions in assets/examples/generated. Every normal poster accepted by the QR-download endpoint is also copied into that permanent generated-example directory, while special π sessions continue uploading there directly; Home refreshes the directory when the QR session finishes. Template backgrounds are never substituted as examples. The centerpiece height is 60% of the viewport's shorter side; neighboring cards scale and rotate around it, and cards are culled only after their complete transformed width has left the frame so edge examples never pop out early. The featured card advances every five seconds without running the live demo engine. The existing loading control settles near the bottom as the Play! action, and an empty generated collection simply omits the gallery cards

Typing ∑ from Home opens a moderation grid containing every current cloud example. Its iPad layout presents four portrait posters per row, contains each complete 9:16 thumbnail, and explicitly centers the artwork so the middle visitor content is prioritized rather than an upper-edge crop; narrow phones use two columns. Tapping a card toggles its inclusion state; excluded cards are visibly dimmed and can always be tapped again to restore them. The DOM moderation overlay stops touch, pointer, and mouse events before they reach p5's global input handlers, preserving native iPad tapping and vertical scrolling. Done writes the shared identifier list to moderation/home-exclusions.json in the bound R2 bucket through POST /api/examples/moderation, then immediately filters the Home carousel. GET /api/examples returns the same exclusions so every kiosk and iPad restores the shared state on reload; localStorage under playspace.hidden-home-examples.v1 remains only a temporary fallback cache. Cancel or Escape discards the draft, failures keep the grid open with a retry message, and no poster/example image object is deleted. The moderation JSON intentionally shares the bucket's one-day lifecycle because its identifiers are no longer relevant after the corresponding example PNGs expire

The local Mac server exposes a phone-oriented controller at /control/ following Wetware's operator pattern without adding a keyboard or external service. It shows dedicated QR codes and URLs for ipad-1 and ipad-2, remembers each scanned device identity locally, and reports both kiosks online through a persistent server-sent event connection. The phone can target either iPad or both and remotely invoke π seed mode or the ∑ Home-gallery moderation screen; the ø demo viewer remains keyboard-only and is intentionally absent from the controller. Each kiosk acknowledges whether the action was accepted in its current scene and returns its current secret-mode state; the compact output/kiosk-runtime server includes the same controller protocol and page

The card begins at neutral 50% grey. The former background-doodle pipeline is removed. The 500px UI-scaled p5 hue dial sits behind and below the Rehumanize button, sharing its horizontal center on the active control side while retaining its bottom-gutter vertical center and rise-in transition. It behaves like a lucky-draw wheel with drag momentum, inertial slowdown, and six-color snapping; exact RGB bypasses glass. Its IDEAFEST-inspired silhouette uses 18 irregular ten-point brush wedges, a 300-degree fan, elevated inner opening, settle-only selected-disk morph, and subtle rotating radial nudges. The live bottom sample drives the background before snapping among F79D1F, CDDD46, DBDCDA, 7BCBBB, C1BEDF, and 4D1430

The selected dial wedge's settle morph is reversible and cohesive: its broad outer geometry contracts up to 15% toward the inner anchor with stronger influence toward the cap, slightly leading but overlapping the simultaneous ten-point circle morph; reversing restores the circle into the contracted wedge while naturally relaxing its outer width and length. The cached dial texture is reused once beneath itself as a zero-black fake shadow at 20% opacity and 2 depth units behind the exact silhouette, adding no duplicate geometry generation. Its offset retains a constant 8 UI-scaled pixel magnitude while its angle eases along the shortest arc to point directly away from the cursor, treating the pointer as a lightweight moving light source

The current fixed 4:5 foreground overlay at assets/poster/overlay/foreground.svg is centered and scaled exactly to the nested creation-card bounds above visitor content and included as the frontmost Card Preview layer; foreground_old.svg is retained only as the retired source. The active 1080x1350 vector is cache-busted and split once at load into unchanged multicolored artwork and a white mask from its identifiable Text path, accepting either hexadecimal or rgb fill styles. A lightweight tint eases that mask continuously between #1d1d1d and white without rebuilding the SVG or fading the colored graphics. Rendering samples two pixels inside each source edge and explicitly disables strokes so transparent-edge filtering cannot introduce a dark seam. DBDCDA, 7BCBBB, and CDDD46 target dark foreground while F79D1F, C1BEDF, and 4D1430 target light foreground; during dial motion the nearest palette anchor updates the eased target

Start opens a dimmed front camera UI with a mirrored live preview and rounded frame; its title is chosen randomly on each opening from the newline-separated assets/data/camera_capture_labels.txt list without repeating the immediately previous title, while Take and Cancel emerge from behind the preview and reverse behind it on exit, with camera-stream cleanup when the prompt closes

The live Take Photo view displays the supplied high-resolution head-and-shoulders guide centered and proportionally contained inside the rounded camera preview. The guide layout is recalculated from the current viewfinder on every frame so portrait, landscape, and window resizing cannot push it out of bounds. It is a UI overlay only, remains visible during the countdown, and hides from the captured-photo review and exported image. A 24x18 preview sample updates perceived average luminance about four times per second; dark scenes crossfade to assets/ui/camera/face_marking_light.svg, bright scenes crossfade to assets/ui/camera/face_marking.svg, and 46%-54% hysteresis prevents lighting noise from flickering the outline. Both files render as native browser SVG elements above the low-density p5 canvas, preserving sharp Retina and iPad edges while crossfading their opacity without raster recoloring

Typing π enables a local seed-recording mode. Start then chooses one of twelve expanded prepared portraits and generates a two-word Indonesian name. The female and male pools retain high-confidence names, while ambiguous forms such as Sri, Nur, Ade, Andi, Dede, Wayan, Wahyu, Dian, Fitri, Ari, Dwi, Tri, and Rizki stay in the in-between pool. Explicit counterpart rules normalize both name parts, including Indra/Indri, Agung/Ageng, Yanto/Yanti, Irianto/Irianti, Putra/Putri, and common -wan/-wati pairs. The flow jumps directly to frame drawing; Finish remembers the special-session state before recipe capture clears its recording flag, stores the normalized frame, per-word name paths, face asset/category, and word-length pattern as compact JSON in the per-device playspace.secret-recipes.v1 collection, and uploads the flattened final poster to assets/examples/generated for the Home carousel

Typing ø from Idle opens the newest locally saved π demo. On each load it replaces every displayed name part with a random gender-compatible candidate whose character count is within one of the recorded word, remapping the original paths and layer keys only in memory so the saved JSON remains unchanged. The existing phase player replays its framed portrait and remapped name paths without normal editing controls; Left and Right Arrow wrap through previous and next records, while ø or Escape closes the viewer

Camera startup uses iPad-friendly ideal front-camera constraints with a plain-video fallback, requires a secure HTTPS context, includes playsinline and webkit-playsinline playback hints, and reports actionable permission, installed-app, missing-camera, or busy-camera errors
Successful camera capture plays assets/audio/camera_capture.m4a and flashes the screen behind the frozen rounded viewfinder

After capture, the frozen viewfinder remains open with vertically stacked Next, Retake, and Cancel controls; Retake is red and immediately runs another countdown, while only the green Next control accepts the photo before editing, removes the underlying idle Start control, and confirms through one continuous downward card sweep that hides each stationary button before it stops rendering

After accepting a photo, visitors draw a freehand frame inside a large dedicated 4:5 work card before editing; the same artwork is nested into the final 9:16 poster only after the creative stage. The captured photo remains visible as a 39%-opacity full-card reference while drawing and becomes fully opaque only inside the completed mask; there is no separate photo avatar. The frame drawing and review screens intentionally omit Exit, leaving the top-right Humanize countdown timer, centered title, branded card overlay, and bottom closed-loop instruction. Only while the frame remains open, the native mouse cursor is replaced by assets/ui/icons/draw_cursor.png with subtle rings; it follows the pointer, hides its Touch and drag anywhere label during drawing or movement, and reveals that label below the hand after 450ms idle. Its outer and card colors derive from the session's randomly selected six-color palette rather than a fixed maroon. Unfinished releases preserve the path for continuation; returning within a 64px start-point radius force-closes it with a lightly jittered connector, and review restores the native cursor and offers side-by-side Next and Redraw controls
Closed photo frames remain fully freehand: the path receives one mild smoothing pass with no template recognition, predetermined shapes, or magnetic pull
Each captured portrait may still be checked locally in the browser with MediaPipe Face Detector, but the visitor's closed frame is never altered: the exact path they draw remains the crop boundary

The freehand frame combines a smooth organic outline with an independently seeded triadic accent snapped to a 16px grid; both follow the same underlying path with a cohesive jelly animation built from two broad traveling lobes, five restrained detail lobes, slow whole-shape breathing, and slight tangential sway, producing prominent but non-chaotic motion while the accent retains rounded joins and occasional diagonal connections
Semantic green actions use RGB (125, 150, 100), while semantic red actions use RGB (255, 100, 125), converted to equivalent HSV values for the glass UI shader

During frame drawing the captured portrait remains fixed beneath the visitor's path. Confirmation freezes the exact photo placement and preserves the visitor's frame coordinates relative to the 4:5 card; it no longer recenters or fits the finished sticker. Layout transitions remap the photo and mask together from the actual prior card bounds, including window resize, so their relative placement remains stable and inside the card

Frame confirmation immediately enters text editing, focuses the hidden input, invokes the iPad keyboard, and keeps both animated frame outlines legible over the fixed grey background with a white primary stroke

The former expandable XY texture pad is replaced by one compact, visually stationary glass REHUMANIZE button, vertically centered on the active control side and mirrored with the rest of the editor. Every release makes the complete rendered name cycle quickly through texture seeds, visibly slow, then settle on one persisted result; the control itself retains only its normal pressed feedback and does not spin or animate during randomization. Only the settled shuffle seed enters editor history, keeping each cycle a single undoable change. Glyph positions from every word are randomized as one collection, then assigned only among the families available for that letter while continually preferring the least-used family. This keeps Airbrush, Pastel, Collage, and Marker as visually even as the supplied character assets allow, prevents short words from independently over-weighting one family, and falls back to the plain font only when no scanned version of a character exists

The layer stack is aligned immediately above Rehumanize on the same control side and titled Layers. Every name word has a labeled, reorderable row with a three-bar handle; the selected row uses assets/ui/containers/layers_active.svg, idle rows use layers_idle.svg, and the locked Photo row uses layers_locked.svg. The stack compacts vertically on landscape viewports and continuously tracks the Rehumanize button width and handedness transition. Frontmost remains at top, background taps collapse selection, and vertical dragging changes plain Z order. Canvas, text bar, Rehumanize, and rows retain bidirectional word selection without opening the iPad keyboard

Right-handed mode is the default: balanced artboard workspace left, all editing panels right. A circular glass '<' switch begins bottom-left opposite the controls. Pressing it starts a reversible live mirror animation: Rehumanize, Layers, Wheel, switch button, artboard, photo, and text continuously cross to their opposite positions while the label changes to '>'; the reverse transition is equally smooth. The preference is persisted under localStorage key playspace.control-side.v1 only after the transition settles, preventing mid-animation cache mismatch. All side controls and the switch hide on Done while the artboard returns to center

Take Picture runs a three-second 3-2-1 countdown with repeated colored numerals moving over the current gradient workspace behind the camera card. The camera and review layout uses a top-left Exit slice, centered PlaySpace logo and heading, a rounded preview, and side-by-side Retake and Next slices. Exit opens the supplied Back to Home confirmation artwork with Cancel and Yes actions. With p5 angle mode kept in degrees, the number grid moves continuously along a randomized base angle for 3, then related +120-degree and -120-degree angles for 2 and 1; each new countdown chooses a base at least 90 degrees from the previous one. Rising synthesized notes remain configurable as major, harmonic, or harmonicMinor in scene.session.camera.countdown.scale

Captured photos fill their visitor-drawn frame on the creative canvas and become their own sticker layer in Card Preview; Cancel, Escape, or a background tap returns to editing without clearing, while successful Finish ends the session and returns to idle Start

A new session starts empty with one randomly selected exact color from the six-color background palette, excluding the immediately previous session color so a fresh assignment is always visible, unless an unfinished localStorage and IndexedDB session is restored after refresh; the photo, frame, text, size, colors, and texture coordinates survive reload, while successful digital-card confirmation is the finish boundary

Finishing the background picker now captures the final poster without showing a separate confirmation scene and opens the QR-download handoff directly. The QR scene fills the entire safe viewport with the same single CSS gradient as the page, with no nested 9:16 scene border or container shadow. It contains a larger centered interactive 9:16 result sized up to 90% of the content width or 35% of the container height, with the poster area reserving a 17% lower gutter for the QR and Finish row so the rotating card nearly fills its available space without sitting beneath surrounding UI. Its front is the exported poster and its back uses the matching clean 01-06 graphic from assets/poster/back/backgrounds beneath the transparent assets/poster/back/card_back_side.png artwork. Backside graphics render with centered cover cropping so the slightly shorter fourth source is never stretched. It performs one presentation spin, then supports horizontal pointer dragging, release inertia, and front-or-back snapping. The QR, countdown, and Finish action sit as a foreground overlay above the card, retaining their own hit areas without disabling card interaction elsewhere. Shared hidden-position helpers move transitioning controls a full control extent plus padding beyond every viewport edge so exported button slices cannot bleed in before their reveal

The two-minute creation timer begins on entry to frame drawing and continues through editing and redraws. Timeout acts as Finish: it automatically completes an unfinished frame with a safe full-card fallback and advances to background selection. Exit is unavailable during frame drawing and frame review, then returns in the active editor with the full-screen Back to Home confirmation. During editing, the enlarged 4:5 work card and its outer-tint cutout stay 4:5, the name field expands across the top, Undo and Redo restore editor snapshots, Delete clears every text path without deleting the typed name or photo, and Next sits at bottom center between the occupied left and right controls. Next transitions directly into the background-frame carousel without an intermediate non-editing scene; the carousel's Edit action and Escape return directly to editing

All p5 edge-anchored controls read the iPad safe-area environment insets through shared top and bottom helpers. Camera, frame drawing, editor, background picker, preview, demo, and handedness controls keep their existing visual padding in addition to clearing the status area and Home indicator; full-bleed backgrounds remain unchanged. The DOM QR handoff uses the same safe-area contract and constrains its rotating card inside the remaining height. The fixed HTML container, canvas, and QR safe-area strip use a CSS reconstruction of the exact p5 Home gradient: the same diagonal base stops and the same cream and pink radial centers and radii. The canvas fills its container with percentage sizing rather than iPad Safari's inconsistent 100dvh, preventing a differently colored bottom strip. Bottom editing controls now interpolate between absolute safe visible and fully off-screen positions instead of adding a fixed offset that became too small when the Home-indicator inset moved their visible anchor upward. Browser builds of p5 1.11.13 and p5.sound are committed under vendor/ and loaded through relative URLs, allowing both the Node kiosk server and a static /PlaySpace/ deployment to start without domain-root /vendor routes. Small parser-blocking fallback scripts load the identical pinned version from jsDelivr only when a local bundle is absent, preserving local-first event operation while allowing an incomplete static demo deployment to recover

Carousel Finish opens the large rotating final-card confirmation. Its Finish action exports a flattened 1440x2560 (9:16) PNG. The final kiosk page shows the completed poster in the center, places its unique download QR and Scan QR to save poster label at bottom-left, runs a visible 60-second scan countdown, and places a teal Finish action at bottom-right. The optional PlaySpace Wi-Fi join QR remains supported when configured, poster sessions expire after 15 minutes by default, and p5 plus QR generation are served locally rather than from runtime CDNs; the pre-existing optional MediaPipe camera helper remains externally sourced. The active handoff URL and stage persist across page reloads, and the creative session is cleared by Finish or when the 60-second scan window expires

The kiosk interface and all creative assets are served locally from the Mac. The readable source and public Invinixity demo retain the personal Cloudflare endpoint declared in js/runtime_config.js, while npm run build:kiosk:ideafest overrides only the generated M1 event runtime to use https://poster.ideafest.id. The deployed IdeaFest custom domain has valid HTTPS, accepts the event origin https://playspace.local:8443, and reports an active R2 binding through /health. The Worker source is tracked in cloudflare-worker/worker.js and accesses the private playspace-posters R2 bucket through the POSTERS binding. It accepts origin-restricted PNG uploads up to 20 MB, returns public QR download and poster-image URLs, streams private objects through the Worker, retains up to 50 recent R2-backed Home examples, and records a 24-hour expiry matching the bucket's one-day lifecycle cleanup. If the complete cloud handoff fails or exceeds 15 seconds, the kiosk automatically posts the finished PNG to the Mac server instead and displays the Mac's Bonjour .local download URL as the QR; both source and compact kiosk servers retain these local sessions for 15 minutes. Browser QR generation is bundled in vendor/qrcode.min.js so neither path depends on an external QR service

The standalone M1 event runtime supports HTTPS directly when PLAYSPACE_TLS_CERT and PLAYSPACE_TLS_KEY are configured, defaulting securely to port 8443 while retaining plain HTTP port 8080 for development without TLS variables. The event Mac advertises playspace.local, and all kiosk, controller, device, and local poster-fallback URLs inherit the active HTTPS protocol. Its event certificate and private key live outside the runtime under ~/Library/Application Support/PlaySpace so runtime updates cannot overwrite them. A per-user launchd service at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.invinixity.playspace.plist starts the zero-dependency runtime at login, restarts it after failure, and records output in ~/Library/Logs/PlaySpace without running Node as root
Developer alignment guides toggle with Shift+/ (?) and follow the pointer with red horizontal and vertical lines

npm run build:kiosk creates a generated, self-contained event copy at output/kiosk-runtime without changing the readable source project. The runtime combines the ordered PlaySpace browser globals into one minified app.min.js without a source map, minifies style.css, retains only currently used assets and expanded portraits, and downsamples the 129 scan glyph PNGs to their existing 512px runtime target. It includes a zero-dependency Node static server, so npm start works directly inside that folder without npm install or node_modules. The public poster endpoint is compiled from js/runtime_config.js, so the runtime must be rebuilt after that domain changes
nextPriorities: Design a start-to-finish public kiosk session with reset and inactivity timeout
Validate the layered digital-card finish and memory use on iPadOS
Continue performance profiling on tablet hardware as assets and effects increase
continuationInstructions: Work from the repository root, then modify only creators/louism/PlaySpace unless explicitly requested otherwise.
Run git status and inspect existing diffs before editing; never discard uncommitted user work.
Keep the current global p5 architecture unless a requested change clearly justifies refactoring.
Test visual changes at desktop, iPad portrait, and a narrow mobile viewport.
Do not commit or push until the user requests it.

development.notes: npm start serves the kiosk UI and all assets from the Mac. Poster uploads, QR downloads, and the Home example gallery normally use the Cloudflare endpoint configured in js/runtime_config.js. When cloud poster delivery is unavailable, the kiosk and scanning phone must share the Mac's local network for the automatic Bonjour fallback QR to work. Validate rendering, console output, touch/mouse interaction, audio startup, Loading-to-Start, camera permission/live capture/cancel, editing, and the perspective Card Preview manually.

worktreeAtLastUpdate.status: Uncommitted local changes include the Loading-to-Start session flow, camera capture, and print-preview implementation. Inspect git diff for the authoritative current state.
